supporting_observations.claim: The HTTPS connections from about 13:40 to 14:10 UTC recur at roughly five-minute intervals and target updates.pixelforge-suite.com, matching the approved PixelForge updater service in the supplied inventory.

Endpoint network telemetry attributes the successful PixelForge update connections to C:\Program Files\PixelForge\pfupdater.exe (PID 4812); the process was launched from the user's Explorer session and created a temporary MSI file.
The 13:45 PixelForge connection was denied by the proxy with status 407; the other listed updater attempts received status 200.

The 13:30 HTTPS connection went to res.cdn.office.net and the 13:43 connection went to outlook.office365.com, services consistent with the organization's approved Microsoft 365 use; these records do not establish that either connection was part of the PixelForge updater cadence.
WS-LMARTINS-01 made SMB connections to FILE-NWD-01 at 13:55 and 14:03, and FILE-NWD-01 logged the corresponding sessions as ANONYMOUS LOGON over NTLM.

At 14:11, DC-NWD-01 initiated a TCP connection to WS-LMARTINS-01 on port 135. This is unexplained by the supplied remote-administration practice, which specifies WS-SOKAFOR-01 as the remote administration workstation; the connection record alone does not show what action, if any, followed.
WmiPrvSE.exe ran on WS-LMARTINS-01 from about 13:46:49 to 14:11:23, but the available records do not link that process to the DC's port-135 connection or establish remote execution.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show HTTPS CONNECT destinations and tunnel byte counts, not the encrypted URLs, requests, or response contents.
The SMB records establish connections and anonymous logons, but do not identify the accessed shares, files, or operations.
The port-135 connection records do not identify the remote procedure, caller's intent, or any resulting process execution.
claims_not_established: Whether the SMB sessions to FILE-NWD-01 accessed an authorized resource or performed any sensitive action.
Whether the DC-NWD-01 connection to WS-LMARTINS-01 was authorized and what RPC/WMI activity, if any, resulted.

Whether any activity in the window was malicious; the PixelForge HTTPS pattern itself is well explained by the approved updater, but the separate SMB and remote-management activity remains unresolved.
additional_evidence_needed: FILE-NWD-01 SMB share-access and object-access auditing for the two sessions, including share names, paths, and operations.
WS-LMARTINS-01 WMI and RPC operational logs, process creation/parent-child telemetry, and DC-NWD-01 records identifying the source process and account for the port-135 activity.
Change or management records confirming whether the DC-to-workstation connection and FILE-NWD-01 SMB sessions were authorized.
